usefulness.rationale: The dossier consistently and multiply corroborates the core identity: Anders Danielsson as Skanska's President/CEO, backed by independent sources (CNBC video pages, ENR, Yahoo Finance, Nasdaq) spanning 2019–2026, plus concrete activities — announcing a 3,000-person global workforce reduction as new CEO (ENR), and repeated media appearances discussing earnings, inflation/interest-rate mitigation, war-in-Ukraine price pressures, AI use in infrastructure planning, and data-centre/residential development. A reader learns who he is and what he has actually done, but the dossier is thin on personal biography (education, pre-CEO career path, tenure start date) — those details exist only in the identity anchors, not in cited dossier claims. Nothing in the dossier states what it does not know: there is no gaps/limitations section, and several claims carry only 'claimed' status without acknowledged uncertainty, so it mildly implies more completeness than it has — hence a low-but-not-zero remainingQuestions score. For meeting prep, the topical currency is genuinely useful (his public positions on macro pressures, US operations stability, AI adoption through mid-2026), though it offers little on his priorities, negotiation style, or background. Notably, none of the three listed unjustified conclusions (Migration Agency role, company revenue/emissions as personal output, FT Best Employer award) appear anywhere in the dossier statements, so there is nothing to match them against; my scan of each claim against its own cited quote found no statement asserting more than its passage supports — the closest cases (the 2021 'good year' claim and the 'as CEO' macro-pressure claim) are supported by their sources' titles even though the quoted excerpts alone are sparser, so I did not flag them.
